hook.text: A band of towering thunderstorms wraps around the entire equator—this is the Intertropical Convergence Zone.

buildup.text: Trade winds from both hemispheres converge here, forcing warm, moist air upward in a belt of heavy rain.

discovery.text: The ITCZ shifts north and south with the seasons—following the Sun's most direct rays.

twist.text: Over oceans, the ITCZ usually sits north of the equator—because the Northern Hemisphere has more landmass to heat.

climax.text: Sailors called this zone the doldrums—winds die here, and ships could be becalmed for weeks.

punchline.text: The rainiest belt on Earth once stranded sailing ships.

quiz.question: Why do the trade winds converge at the ITCZ?
options: Warm air rises, pulling surface winds inward
